description: The figure presents two horizontal bar charts comparing the “% point difference” in morphosyntactic probing performance across layers of the XLM-R model, likely contrasting two different probing setups or model variants (as suggested by the differing bar colors: light blue in the top chart and dark blue in the bottom). Both charts share the same x-axis labeled “layer,” ranging from 0 to 12, followed by a “concat” category, and the same y-axis labeled “% point difference,” scaled from 0 to –10 in increments of 2. In the top chart (light blue bars), layer 0 shows the largest negative difference at approximately –10.5%, followed by layer 1 at ~–8.5%, layer 2 at ~–7.5%, layer 3 at ~–5.5%, layer 4 at ~–4.5%, and layer 5 at ~–2.5%. Layers 6 through 11 show progressively smaller negative differences, ranging from ~–1.5% to nearly 0%, while layer 12 dips to ~–2% and “concat” rises slightly above 0%. The bottom chart (dark blue bars) mirrors this trend closely: layer 0 at ~–10%, layer 1 at ~–9%, layer 2 at ~–8%, layer 3 at ~–6%, layer 4 at ~–4%, layer 5 at ~–2.5%, with layers 6–11 hovering near –1% to 0%, layer 12 at ~–1%, and “concat” slightly positive. The consistent negative values suggest a performance drop relative to a baseline, with early layers (0–5) showing the most significant degradation, and later layers and the concatenated representation approaching parity or slight improvement. The label “XLM-R” centered between the two charts indicates the model under analysis, and the near-identical patterns suggest the two charts may represent different probing tasks, languages, or experimental conditions within the same model architecture.
